_comment: Curated, not exhaustive. Each entry is a real RPython helper with a precondition its signature doesn't enforce -- calling it with an out-of-precondition value produces PyPy's generic 'SystemError: unexpected internal exception (please report a bug)' leak instead of a proper app-level exception. Seeded from danzin's fusil findings (docs/PYPY_FINDINGS_REPORT.md); grow this list from future confirmed bugs, not speculation. See design doc §9.1. A helper whose precondition has independent clauses declares them in `clauses`: each is discharged separately, by a call-site keyword (`discharged_by_kwarg`), by a proactive text hint, or by a reactive `except` handler -- and a reactive guard counts only when EVERY name in `exception_guard_hints` is handled, since a partial handler is exactly the shape of confirmed bug #3. A call leaving ANY clause undischarged stays CONSIDER -- a range check must not clear a surrogate obligation. Helpers with no `clauses` key keep the original single-clause behaviour.

helpers.precondition: argument must be <= 0x10FFFF and, unless allow_surrogates=True is passed, not a surrogate (0xD800-0xDFFF)
helpers.confirmed_bug: struct.unpack('u', b'abcd') -- pypy/module/struct/formatiterator.py's append_utf8 passes r_uint(value) straight through with no range check at all. Second confirmed instance, surrogate clause only: format(0xD800, 'c') / f'{0xD800:c}' -- pypy/objspace/std/newformat.py:847 range-checks 0 <= value <= 0x10FFFF three lines above the call but omits allow_surrogates=True, so the 2048 surrogate codepoints pass the guard and leak SystemError. Reproduced on PyPy 7.3.23 (194f9f44b505); CPython 3.14.4 returns '\ud800'. Same shape reproduced in pypy/module/_csv/interp_csv.py via csv.reader(iter([]), delimiter='\ud800').

helpers.precondition: the 'signed' argument must actually match whether the bigint's value is negative -- passing signed=False (or leaving a stale/attacker-controlled state) for a negative value raises an internal OverflowError-shaped RPython exception, not the app-level OverflowError CPython raises
helpers.confirmed_bug: codecs.getincrementalencoder(<multibyte codec>)().setstate(-1) -- the state int is handed to rbigint.tobytes() with no sign check first

helpers.precondition: same as rbigint.tobytes -- module-level variant taking a plain int rather than an rbigint instance
helpers.confirmed_bug: same underlying shape as rbigint.tobytes; not itself the confirmed call site but sharing the same precondition
